findings.issue: Repeatedly prefixed commands with `pkill -f '.output/server/index.mjs'`, whose pattern matches the agent's own bash command line, killing the shell (exit 143) before the build/test could run — four times, costing a turn each time and two wasted test invocations.
findings.suggestion: Kill by exact process (`pkill -xf 'node .output/server/index.mjs'`), store the server PID at start, or use `fuser -k`/a distinct marker; diagnose a repeated exit code on its second occurrence, not in the final turn.

findings.issue: The app is TypeScript but no typecheck was ever run; Vite 8's oxc-based build does not surface type errors, so type mistakes would ship silently.
findings.suggestion: Add `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"` to app/package.json and run it before declaring done.

findings.issue: The visual pass skipped /abilities/static and /?type=fire&generation=generation-i, two pages the spec explicitly asks to match against reference screenshots.
findings.suggestion: Screenshot every URL listed in the spec's screenshot table, at both widths.

findings.issue: Reconstructed the official SolidStart template by listing the GitHub tree and curl-ing files one at a time over ~8 turns.
findings.suggestion: Clone the template dir once (`npx degit solidjs/templates solid-start-v2/basic`) or fetch a tarball in a single command.

findings.issue: Read the spec and test files through bash `cat`/`sed -n` instead of the read tool, and several early bash calls bundled multiple reads into one giant output.
findings.suggestion: Use the read tool with offsets for large text files so output truncation is controlled.

summary: An exemplary autonomous run: exhaustive upfront discovery (spec, tests, data shapes, overlay, screenshots), framework version verified against npm instead of memory, one giant planning block executed almost verbatim, and the single real bug root-caused and fixed in three turns. Verification went beyond the tests with screenshot-by-screenshot visual comparison at both widths and a full re-run after the final edit. The only meaningful flaw is four self-inflicted `pkill` shell kills it kept repeating without diagnosing, plus no typecheck on a TypeScript app.
